legal.headline: Sohrabuddin case: Supreme Court says it will not reopen Amit Shah's discharge but seeks CBI reply on plea against acquittal of others
legal.hook: Sohrabuddin case: Supreme Court says it will not reopen Amit Shah's discharge but seeks CBI reply on plea against acquittal of others
legal.summary: The Supreme Court has declined to revisit its earlier discharge of Amit Shah in the 2005 Sohrabuddin Sheikh fake encounter case, but has called for a CBI response to a plea challenging the acquittal of other accused persons in the same matter. The Court's order indicates a bifurcated stance: finality on Shah's discharge (granted in 2014 by the Gujarat High Court, upheld by the Supreme Court) versus openness to scrutiny of the acquittals of co-accused. The CBI has been asked to file its reply, suggesting the bench may be considering whether grounds exist to challenge the trial court's acquittal findings. The case involves the 2005 extrajudicial killing of gangster Sohrabuddin Sheikh and his wife Kauser Bi in Gujarat. No date for the next hearing or substantive decision has been reported in the excerpt.
legal.contextNote: This touches the intersection of finality in criminal discharge under CrPC §227 (discharge at committal) versus challenge to acquittal under §378 CrPC (appeal by the State). Shah's discharge at the committal stage is treated as final and unreviewable once upheld by an appellate forum; however, the acquittals of co-accused are substantive judgments post-trial, which remain challengeable. The distinction matters: discharge orders have heightened finality protection (*Balaji Sathe v. State of Maharashtra*, 2015 SCC Online SC 1043). For in-house counsel tracking political/law enforcement risk: (1) this signals the Court's willingness to scrutinize trial outcomes even in high-profile cases years after judgment, (2) the CBI's response will reveal whether the agency has identified specific grounds (procedural, evidential, or interpretive) to mount an appeal against acquittal, and (3) any reversal of acquittals would be rare and fact-specific, not a blanket reopening.

retail.headline: High prices this sale season is a done deal, but that's only half the story
retail.hook: For retailers, the festive strategy this year will shift from outright price cuts towards a combination of financing, product redesign, wider entry-level choices and exchange offers, with the aim to preserve margins…
retail.summary: Retailers in India are adjusting their strategies for the festive season, moving away from traditional price cuts to a multifaceted approach that includes financing options, product redesigns, and a broader range of entry-level products. This shift aims to maintain profit margins while accommodating consumer purchasing despite elevated prices. This strategy reflects a response to the ongoing inflationary pressures affecting consumer spending habits.

retail.headline: 89 per cent of Meesho Mall's new-to-brand shoppers came from smaller cities in FY26: Milan Partani

The data suggests a robust demand for affordable and accessible products in smaller urban areas, which could influence future marketing and product development strategies for brands operating on Meesho Mall.
retail.contextNote: This trend aligns with the provisions of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, particularly Section 2(1)(c), which defines 'consumer' broadly, encompassing individuals from diverse demographics. As Meesho Mall continues to attract consumers from smaller cities, in-house counsel should (1) review compliance with e-commerce regulations under the Information Technology Act, 2000, especially regarding data protection and consumer rights; (2) monitor advertising practices to ensure they meet the standards set by the Advertising Standards Council of India (ASCI); and (3) assess supply chain logistics to cater to the increasing demand from these regions, ensuring that products meet local preferences and regulatory requirements.

retail.headline: Rado steps up premium play in India as Swiss watch market grows 31 pc
retail.hook: Rado, a Swiss watchmaker, is witnessing remarkable growth in India, marking it as its largest market globally.
retail.summary: Rado, a Swiss watchmaker, has reported a 31% growth in its market in India, making it the brand's largest global market. retail.headline: Festive shopping gets costlier as brands plan to hike AC, TV and appliance prices from October 1

retail.hook: Large food companies and restaurants are expanding their hiring for food safety and compliance roles.
retail.summary: In response to intensified inspections by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), large food companies and restaurant chains in India are significantly increasing their recruitment for food safety and compliance roles. retail.headline: Swiss Beauty Select targets Rs 100 crore as premium beauty arm charts 100 pc plus growth

world.headline: Eviction of 87-year-old sparks protests in Madrid over housing crisis
world.hook: Tens of thousands marched through Madrid on Saturday to protest Spain's housing crisis and the eviction of an 87-year-old woman, camping overnight in Madrid's historic Puerta del Sol plaza.

Activists camped overnight in the plaza, demanding urgent government action to address the housing crisis, which has seen a surge in evictions amid rising rents and property prices. The Spanish government has pledged to implement measures to regulate the rental market, but activists argue that these steps are insufficient to protect vulnerable residents from eviction.

world.summary: In a troubling series of incidents, South Africa experienced mass shootings that resulted in the deaths of 38 individuals within a single week. Authorities have not yet apprehended any suspects, and the police have launched investigations into these violent acts. South African President Cyril Ramaphosa condemned the violence, emphasizing the need for urgent action to combat crime and restore safety in communities.
